title: Wood Mackenzie: Strong Balance Sheets Set 2027 Up for Oil and Gas Portfolio Renewal
gist: Most large oil and gas companies enter 2027 with gearing below 20% after 2026's price and margin surge, funding a 5% investment rise and a fresh M&A wave. The structural driver is a 31%, or 18 mmboe/d, production decline between 2030 and 2040 across Wood Mackenzie's five peer groups excluding Middle Eastern NOCs, forcing a 2027 planning cycle defined by the tension between capital discipline and upstream portfolio renewal.

themes.theme: Balance sheet strength and the 2027 capital cycle

insights.claim: Most large oil and gas companies will enter 2027 with gearing below 20%, following accelerated deleveraging driven by surging prices and margins in 2026.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Sub-20% gearing is the dry powder that funds the 2027 M&A wave; balance-sheet capacity, not price, becomes the swing variable for deal flow.
insights.quote: Most large oil and gas companies will enter 2027 with gearing below 20%, following accelerated deleveraging driven by surging prices and margins in 2026

insights.claim: The sector's financial position creates the platform for a 5% rise in investment, a fresh wave of M&A, and resource renewal aimed at sustaining production into the 2030s.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A 5% capex uplift is a modest, disciplined number: bullish for oilfield services volumes but not a return to boom-era spending.
insights.quote: That financial position creates the platform for a 5% rise in investment, a fresh wave of M&A, and the resource renewal aimed at sustaining production into the 2030s.

insights.claim: Capital discipline will hold even at Brent prices above Wood Mackenzie's US$73 per barrel base case, rather than higher prices triggering a spending surge.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Breaks the historic price-to-capex reflex: upside in oil prices should flow to shareholder returns and deleveraging, not drilling budgets.
insights.quote: Capital discipline will hold, even at Brent prices above Wood Mackenzie's US$73 per barrel base case.

insights.claim: Reinvestment rates in 2027 will average 50% of operating cash flow, with distributions accounting for 43%, split 32% dividends and 11% buybacks.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The dividend-heavy 32/11 split signals a preference for base payout stability over opportunistic buybacks, relevant for equity income positioning.
insights.quote: Reinvestment rates in 2027 will average 50% of operating cash flow; distributions account for 43%, split 32% dividends and 11% buybacks.

insights.claim: The peer group will require US$55 per barrel on average to break even after investment and dividends, providing some resilience to lower prices.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: US$55/bbl is the stress line: below it, dividends or capex must give, defining the downside threshold for sector equities.
insights.quote: The group will require US$55 per barrel on average to breakeven after investment and dividends, providing some resilience to lower prices.

insights.claim: Excluding Middle Eastern NOCs, production across Wood Mackenzie's five peer groups declines by 31%, or 18 mmboe/d, between 2030 and 2040.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: An 18 mmboe/d corporate decline by 2040 is the strongest structural argument for long-dated oil price support and for reserve-rich acquisition targets.
insights.quote: Excluding Middle Eastern NOCs, production across Wood Mackenzie's five peer groups declines by 31%, or 18 mmboe/d, between 2030 and 2040.

insights.claim: That post-2030 decline is the structural driver behind the 2027 push for M&A and upstream business development, rather than opportunism about cheap assets.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Deals will be driven by resource-life necessity, which tends to make acquirers price-insensitive and supports target valuations.
insights.quote: That decline is the structural driver behind the 2027 push for M&A and upstream business development.

insights.claim: The defining feature of the 2027 planning cycle is the rising tension companies must manage between capital discipline and upstream portfolio renewal, despite healthy balance sheets.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A clean lens for reading 2027 strategy days: judge management on how they resolve this trade-off, not on headline capex.
insights.quote: Balance sheets are in good shape. But a 31% production decline between 2030 and 2040 means companies will have to manage rising tension between capital discipline and upstream portfolio renewal in 2027.

themes.theme: Price scenarios and cash flow sensitivity

insights.claim: Operating cash flow in 2027 is forecast to remain 14% above 2025 levels at base-case pricing for the peer group.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Base case implies sector cash generation stays structurally above 2025, supporting distributions even without further price upside.
insights.quote: Operating cash flow in 2027 is forecast to remain 14% above 2025 levels at base-case pricing.

insights.claim: At US$90 per barrel, 2027 operating cash flow rises a further 18%, or US$104 billion, while a fall to US$50 per barrel would cut operating cash flow by 24%, or US$138 billion.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Asymmetric sensitivity: the downside dollar swing exceeds the upside, arguing for hedging or defensive positioning into a volatile 2027.
insights.quote: At US$90 per barrel, that figure rises by a further 18%, or US$104 billion. A fall to US$50 per barrel would cut operating cash flow by 24%, or US$138 billion

insights.claim: In a US$50 per barrel scenario, US Majors, Large Cap US, and Large Cap International peer groups face operating cash flow declines of 28% to 29%, the steepest across the sector.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Identifies the most price-levered cohorts to underweight or hedge if oil breaks lower.
insights.quote: with US Majors, Large Cap US, and Large Cap International facing declines of 28% to 29%

insights.claim: Companies will need to plan for a volatile year by building action plans for both upside and downside scenarios rather than a single price deck.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Scenario-flexible capital plans become a differentiator; watch which management teams publish contingent capex triggers.
insights.quote: Companies will need to plan for a volatile year, building in action plans for both upside and downside scenarios.

themes.theme: Capital reallocation, geography and M&A mechanics

insights.claim: Upstream's share of total capital is up eight percentage points since 2021 as Power and Renewables spend, which peaked in 2024, continues to fall.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Confirms a measurable, multi-year reversal of the energy-transition capital shift; renewables developers lose a major source of balance-sheet funding.
insights.quote: Upstream's share of total capital is up eight percentage points since 2021 as Power and Renewables spend, which peaked in 2024, continues to fall.

insights.claim: Two thirds of upstream capital for the peer group flows to the Middle East and the Americas, where tight oil, deepwater and LNG are the dominant growth themes.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Service and equipment demand concentrates in these two regions and three themes; other basins face relative capital starvation.
insights.quote: Two thirds of upstream capital for our peer group flows to the Middle East and the Americas, where tight oil, deepwater, and LNG are the dominant growth themes.

insights.claim: M&A activity levels will depend on whether volatility falls enough for buyers and sellers to align on price, with rising equity valuations giving some companies a financing advantage in equity-led deals.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Falling oil volatility is the leading indicator to watch for a deal wave; highly rated equities are the likely acquirers.
insights.quote: M&A activity levels will depend on whether volatility falls enough for buyers and sellers to align on price. Rising equity valuations give some companies a financing advantage in equity-led deals.

insights.claim: Capital allocation constraints and the pressure to rebuild upstream portfolios for the next decade are already triggering more NOC-IOC partnerships and strategic ventures.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Partnership structures, not outright acquisitions, may be the dominant deal format, changing how resource access should be modelled.
insights.quote: Capital allocation constraints and the pressure to rebuild upstream portfolios for the next decade are already triggering more NOC-IOC partnerships and strategic ventures

insights.claim: Geographic diversification, particularly toward the Americas, will be front of mind as companies respond to shifting geopolitics in 2027.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Expect a bid for Americas-weighted assets and a geopolitical risk discount widening on assets in contested regions.
insights.quote: Geographic diversification, particularly toward the Americas, will be front of mind as companies respond to shifting geopolitics in 2027.

themes.theme: Downstream divergence and the value of flexibility

insights.claim: Refining closures continue in Europe and California, but 2026 exposed how thin the system has become, making the pace of exits a more deliberate question.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A slower refinery rationalisation than consensus assumes would cap the structural upside in refining margins that bulls expect.
insights.quote: Refining closures continue in Europe and California, but 2026 exposed how thin the system has become, making the pace of exits a more deliberate question.

insights.claim: In chemicals, near-term overcapacity is separating companies committing through the trough from those exiting entirely, with feedstock advantage the dividing line.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Use feedstock cost position as the screen for which petrochemical players survive the trough and consolidate share.
insights.quote: In chemicals, near-term overcapacity is separating those committing through the trough from those exiting entirely, with feedstock advantage the dividing line.

insights.claim: The 2027 downstream question is no longer just how fast to shrink but how much flexibility is worth retaining while the system stays tight, even though fundamentals have not changed.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Optionality value in refining and chemical assets is being re-rated upward; asset sales may slow and announced closures may be deferred.
insights.quote: Fundamentals haven't changed, but the 2027 question is no longer just how fast to shrink — it’s how much flexibility is worth retaining while the system stays tight.

themes.theme: Low-carbon recalibration and the NOC reversal

insights.claim: NOCs' low carbon spend is now double that of the Euro Majors, following the latter's strategic recalibration.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Inverts the standard narrative of European leadership on transition spending; national oil companies are now the marginal buyer of low-carbon assets.
insights.quote: NOCs' low carbon spend is now double that of the Euro Majors following the latter’s strategic recalibration.

insights.claim: Most large IOC and NOC low carbon budgets are converging on 5% to 10% of total spend, compared with prior estimates of up to 50% from some Euro Majors at peak ESG guidance levels.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A collapse from up-to-50% guidance to 5-10% actual is the single starkest measure of the transition-capex retreat; recalibrate renewables demand forecasts that assumed oil-major funding.
insights.quote: Most large IOC and NOC low carbon budgets are converging on 5% to 10% of total spend, compared with prior estimates of up to 50% from some Euro Majors at peak ESG guidance levels.

insights.claim: Some players will continue to build out their low-carbon businesses, with TotalEnergies focused on integrated power and Eni leveraging its strategic ventures Plenitude and EniLive.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Names the two European exceptions to the transition retreat; their satellite-vehicle structures are the template for funding low-carbon growth off balance sheet.
insights.quote: some players will continue to build out their low-carbon businesses, with TotalEnergies focused on integrated power and Eni leveraging its strategic ventures Plenitude and EniLive
